accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The proof splits the Euler product for a_k at p=2k^2 so that the small-prime head determines the leading scale and the large-prime tail needs only coarse control. For the upper head, the Mertens-scale factor is accompanied by a residual local-series contribution bounded by exp(O(k^2/log k))=e^{o(k^2)}; the lower head obtains the Mertens-scale product directly. The tail is at most 1, while elementary product inequalities and logarithms reduce its lower bound to a convergent p^(-2) tail, giving e^{o(k^2)}. Matching bounds yield a_k=(e^(-gamma)/(2 log k))^(k^2)e^{o(k^2)} without a sharp tail evaluation.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separate leading-scale mechanism from tail burden in multiplicative coordinates, then take logarithms to turn the tail product into an additive summability estimate.
